introduction: Karma in Jainism is not fate or divine reward — it is a precise, scientific, and moral law of cause and effect governing the soul's journey through infinite lifetimes. Every action, word, and thought generates karmic particles (karma-pudgala) that bind to the soul, influencing future births, experiences, and spiritual capacity. Understanding karma is the key to liberation.
overview: Karma is a subtle form of matter (pudgala) that has the property of existing, of being able to be bound, and of bearing fruit. The soul is pure consciousness, but when it vibrates through action (yoga) under the influence of passions (kashaya), karmic matter flows toward it (asrava) and binds (bandha). The types of karma, their duration, intensity, and quantity depend entirely on the mental and emotional state at the moment of action. Good actions produce pleasant fruits; harmful actions produce suffering. However, even good karma is ultimately a bond that must be shed for liberation.

ghatiyaKarmas.name: Gyanavarniya Karma
ghatiyaKarmas.description: Knowledge-obscuring karma that blocks the soul's infinite knowledge (Kevala Jnana).
ghatiyaKarmas.howToDestroy: Studying scriptures, spiritual reading, and deep meditation destroy knowledge-obscuring karma. The 5 types of knowledge (Mati, Shruta, Avadhi, Manahparyaya, Kevala) progressively shine as this karma is shed.

ghatiyaKarmas.name: Darshanavarniya Karma
ghatiyaKarmas.description: Perception-obscuring karma that dims the soul's infinite perception.
ghatiyaKarmas.howToDestroy: Meditation, stillness (Kayotsarga), and deep contemplation destroy perception-obscuring karma. The soul attains Ananta Darshana (infinite perception) upon complete destruction.

ghatiyaKarmas.name: Mohaniya Karma
ghatiyaKarmas.description: Deluding karma — the most dangerous of all, obscuring right faith and right conduct. It creates attachment, aversion, and spiritual ignorance.
ghatiyaKarmas.howToDestroy: The most stubborn karma, requiring the highest spiritual effort. 28 causes of mithyatva include wrong teacher, wrong scriptural interpretation, weak community, negligence, and carefree attitude. Destroying it requires Samyak Darshana (right faith) and complete eradication of the four kashayas.

ghatiyaKarmas.name: Antaraya Karma
ghatiyaKarmas.description: Obstruction karma that blocks the soul's infinite energy and capacity for liberation.
ghatiyaKarmas.howToDestroy: Generous charity, selfless service, and equanimity in success and failure progressively destroy antaraya karma. When fully destroyed, the soul achieves Ananta Virya (infinite power).

aghatiyaKarmas.name: Vedaniya Karma
aghatiyaKarmas.description: Feeling-producing karma that determines whether experiences are pleasant or painful.
aghatiyaKarmas.howToDestroy: Compassion, self-discipline, and equanimity in pleasure and pain. Monks destroy this karma through severe austerities.

aghatiyaKarmas.name: Nama Karma
aghatiyaKarmas.description: Name/Determination karma that determines physical body, birth, species, and all physical characteristics.

subtypes.name: Sharir Karma
subtypes.desc: Body type: hellish, animal, human, celestial.

aghatiyaKarmas.howToDestroy: Ethical conduct, self-restraint, and monastic discipline destroy name karma. A liberated Siddha has no further nama karma.

aghatiyaKarmas.name: Gotra Karma
aghatiyaKarmas.description: Lineage and status karma determining birth in high/low family, caste, and social standing.
aghatiyaKarmas.howToDestroy: Humility, treating all equally, and destroying pride destroy gotra karma.

aghatiyaKarmas.name: Ayu Karma
aghatiyaKarmas.description: Lifespan karma determining the total lifespan of each birth across the 4 gatis (heavenly, human, animal, hellish).
aghatiyaKarmas.howToDestroy: Ayu karma bears fruit automatically when other karmas mature. Monks destroy it through maximum austerities and equanimity in death (santhara).

subcategories.name: Total Karma Subtypes
subcategories.desc: The 148 total subtypes of karma cover every conceivable variety of experience, covering knowledge, perception, conduct, feeling, body, lineage, lifespan, and spiritual capacity.

subcategories.name: Bandha Mechanism
subcategories.desc: Karma bonds to the soul through yoga (activity of mind, speech, body) combined with kashaya (passions). The stronger the passion, the stronger the bond and the longer the duration.

subcategories.name: Duration of Karma
subcategories.desc: Karma can remain bound from a few minutes to billions of years. The maximum duration for vedaniya karma is 9000 years; for others it ranges from a few minutes to 100 trillion sagaropamas.

subcategories.name: Karma and Free Will
subcategories.desc: Jainism is neither deterministic nor purely existentialist. Past karma conditions present experience, but present action (especially spiritual effort) modifies future karma. The monk who practices Nirjara can shorten even the longest karmic durations.

bandhaMechanism: Bandha (bondage) occurs when karmic matter unites with the soul through four factors: 1) Karma exists (prakriti), 2) The soul is present (ashraya), 3) The soul vibrates through activity (yoga), 4) Passion exists (kashaya) — without passion, karma cannot bond. The four dimensions of bond — nature, quantity, duration, intensity — are determined by the type of activity and the strength of the underlying passions. A monk who has eliminated passions achieves Samvara effortlessly; a passionate layperson creates intense bandha.
nirjaraProcess: Nirjara is the conscious shedding of karmic matter before it bears fruit. It is like washing clothes while they can still be cleaned, rather than wearing them until they are completely worn out. The 12 types of penance (6 external: fasting, reduced diet, renunciation of delicious foods, physical mortification, guarding the body, controlled habitation; 6 internal: atonement, humility, service, scriptural study, meditation, renunciation) systematically dismantle karmic bonds. Progressive Nirjara raises the soul through the 14 Gunasthanaks toward liberation.
householdersGuide: Householders practice Anuvratas (small vows) to limit karmic influx, Gunavratas to develop spiritual merit, and Shikshavratas to cultivate spiritual discipline. The 12 preparatory vows (5 Anuvratas, 3 Gunavratas, 4 Shikshavratas) provide a comprehensive framework for lay spiritual life. Daily Pratikramana, weekly fasting, and annual Paryushan create milestones for karmic purification.
monksGuide: Monks practice the 5 Mahavratas without compromise: total non-violence, total truth, zero stealing, complete celibacy, and total non-possession. Coupled with 5 Samitis and 3 Guptis, monastic life maximizes Samvara and accelerates Nirjara. The monk lives as if already liberated, free of worldly belongings, moving from place to place, sustaining only on alms, and dedicating every moment to spiritual study and meditation. The 28 Mulagunas and 11 Pratimas form the graduated path from householder to monk.
sacredFormula: Jain karma theory can be remembered through the simple formula: ASRAVA → BANDHA → SAMVARA → NIRJARA → MOKSHA. The soul is not a victim of karma but its master, capable of halting influx and actively shedding karmic bonds. This makes Jainism one of the most empowering spiritual systems ever devised.
